# Implementation Types

<!-- purpose: Where Implementation Types files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Implementation data types, one file each under `data_types/implementation/`: how the platform stores the data a model exchanges. Six element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`value_type`, `reference_type`, `external_type`, `implementation_record`, `implementation_array`, `pointer`), plus one nested member kind (`implementation_element`). A `value_type` is the implementation type that rests on a base type, an element of the `base_types` layer, a `reference_type` rests on another implementation type, and `implementation_record`, `implementation_array` and `pointer` are the implementation structure, array and pointer; a mapping set pairs each application type, an element of the `application_types` layer, with the implementation type that stores it. An `external_type` is a stub for an implementation type declared outside the project. An implementation type and an application type may carry one name. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

One file per `implementation_type`, in `data_types/implementation/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

A file of this layer is one of 6 kinds — `value_type`, `reference_type`, `external_type`, `implementation_record`, `implementation_array`, `pointer` — chosen by its `kind` key.

## `value_type` { #value_type }

<!-- purpose: Writing `value_type` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

An implementation data type of category `VALUE`, emitted as an `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` whose `BASE-TYPE-REF` points at its `base`, which must name a declared base type. It is what a data element or an argument names as its type, and what a mapping set pairs with the application type it stores; a record field and an array element name the application view instead. A declared `value_min` or `value_max` is written as the type's own `{name}_Range` `DATA-CONSTR`, one rule of `INTERNAL-CONSTRS` with each declared bound as a `CLOSED` limit, referenced by a `DATA-CONSTR-REF`; `unit` reaches no ARXML element.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `value_type` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `value_type`. |
| `base` | string, the `name` of [base_types](base_types.md) | yes | — | Must name a declared base type, an element of the `base_types` layer. A base type is resolved in that layer alone, so it may carry the value type's own name. |
| `unit` | string | no | `""` | The physical unit of the value, as free text (for example `km/h`). Documentation only; it reaches no ARXML element: Table 5.18 of the software component template gives an implementation data type's `unit` no place in any category, and `[constr_1009]` makes the table binding. |
| `value_min` | number | no | absent | The lower bound of the value; omitted or `null` when there is none. Must be &lt;= `value_max` when both are given; neither accepts NaN or ±Infinity. |
| `value_max` | number | no | absent | The upper bound of the value; omitted or `null` when there is none. Must be >= `value_min` when both are given; neither accepts NaN or ±Infinity. |
| `compu_method_ref` | string, the `name` of [compu_methods](compu_methods.md) | no | absent | The name of a declared `texttable` compu method, an element of the `compu_methods` layer, whose entries name the type's values: the one way an implementation type states literals. Absent states none. Must not be blank. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Implementation`, its layer's package, this value type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the value type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Implementation` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Implementation` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## `reference_type` { #reference_type }

<!-- purpose: Writing `reference_type` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

An implementation data type of category `TYPE_REFERENCE`, emitted as an `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` whose `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE-REF` points at its `base`, which must name a declared `value_type`, another `reference_type`, an `implementation_record`, an `implementation_array`, a `pointer` or an `external_type` stub. It carries no unit and no range: those belong to the `value_type` at the bottom of the chain, and an `init` value under a reference type is judged against the type its chain ends at. Like a value type it is what a data element or an argument names, and what a mapping set pairs with the application type it stores.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `reference_type` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `reference_type`. |
| `base` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | yes | — | Must name a declared value type, reference type, implementation record, implementation array, pointer or external data type stub; may not name the reference type itself, and may not lead back to it through a chain of other types. |
| `compu_method_ref` | string, the `name` of [compu_methods](compu_methods.md) | no | absent | The name of a declared `texttable` compu method, an element of the `compu_methods` layer, whose entries name the type's values: the one way an implementation type states literals. Absent states none. Must not be blank. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Implementation`, its layer's package, this reference type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the reference type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Implementation` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Implementation` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## `external_type` { #external_type }

<!-- purpose: Writing `external_type` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

A stub for an implementation data type declared outside the project: an ARXML export referenced it and declared it nowhere. It carries that reference, `external_ref` and `external_dest`, verbatim and nothing of the type's content. A data element's or an argument's `implementation_type`, a reference type's `base`, an implementation record's element, an implementation array's element and a pointer's `target` may name it, and each is emitted with that reference; a record field, an array element and a mapping set may not. No type is generated for it. Discriminated by `kind: external_type`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `external_type` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `external_type`. |
| `external_ref` | string | no | `""` | The AUTOSAR path the source's type reference carried, verbatim: the type's full path in the file that declares it. Written back unchanged into every reference to the stub. `check-model` reports a blank or malformed one. |
| `external_dest` | string | no | `""` | The `DEST` the source's type reference carried, verbatim. `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` is the one value admitted, and `check-model` reports any other. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the stub. An external stub emits no element, so it reaches no generated artifact. |

## `implementation_record` { #implementation_record }

<!-- purpose: Writing `implementation_record` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

An implementation data type of category `STRUCTURE`, emitted as an `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` whose `SUB-ELEMENTS` are its `elements` in order, each of category `TYPE_REFERENCE` naming the implementation type it carries. Element names are unique inside the type, and an element's type must name a declared implementation type that does not, directly or through other types, contain this type again. A mapping set may pair it with an application record; records are not required to be mapped.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `implementation_record` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `implementation_record`. |
| `elements` | a list of `implementation_element` blocks | yes | — | The type's named, typed elements in declaration order, addressed by `name`. Must not be empty. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Implementation`, its layer's package, this implementation record is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the implementation record and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Implementation` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Implementation` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## `implementation_array` { #implementation_array }

<!-- purpose: Writing `implementation_array` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

An implementation data type of category `ARRAY` with fixed-size semantics: `length` elements of one declared `element_type`, emitted as an `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` with one sub-element named `element_name`. The element type must name a declared implementation type and must not close a cycle back to this array. A mapping set may pair it with an application array; arrays are not required to be mapped. Variable-size arrays are not modelled.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `implementation_array` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `implementation_array`. |
| `element_type` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared type of every element: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub, and never a base type or an application type, enumeration, record or array. It may not be this array itself, nor a type that contains this array. |
| `length` | integer | yes | — | The number of elements in the array, emitted as the sub-element's `ARRAY-SIZE` with `FIXED-SIZE` semantics. Must be > 0. |
| `element_name` | string | yes | — | The `SHORT-NAME` of the array's one sub-element, kept as the source declared it rather than invented. Must not be blank. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Implementation`, its layer's package, this implementation array is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the implementation array and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Implementation` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Implementation` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## `pointer` { #pointer }

<!-- purpose: Writing `pointer` files in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

An implementation data type of category `DATA_REFERENCE`: a pointer to the declared implementation type its `target` names, emitted with `SW-POINTER-TARGET-PROPS` of target category `TYPE_REFERENCE`. A pointer to a pointer names another `pointer` as its target; a pointer graph that leads back to itself is refused. A pointer is never mapped: no mapping set may pair an application type with it, directly, through a reference type or inside a mapped composite. A connector between two application components may not carry a data element or an argument typed by one.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `pointer` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `pointer`. |
| `target` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared type the pointer points to: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub, and never a base type or an application type, enumeration, record or array. It may not name the pointer itself, and may not lead back to it through other types. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Implementation`, its layer's package, this pointer type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the pointer type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Implementation` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Implementation/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Implementation` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Implementation Types files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `implementation_element` { #implementation_element }

<!-- purpose: Writing `implementation_element` blocks in Implementation Types: each key, its type and default -->

A member of an `implementation_record` type's `elements` collection, emitted as one sub-element of category `TYPE_REFERENCE`; like `record_field` it has no file and no layer-level address.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The element's identity inside its implementation record, emitted as the sub-element's `SHORT-NAME`; unique among the record's elements and immutable. |
| `type` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared type the element carries: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub, and never a base type or an application type, enumeration, record or array. It may not close a cycle back to the record. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the implementation element. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
